Hi Aditya,

We're updating our DPA attachments for the upcoming procurement review. Can you send the current subprocessor roster (including network/edge proxies and any caching/KV providers) and clarify whether any of those subprocessors could lead to cross-border storage of end-user content? Specifically:

- For any KV cache provider (session/cache layer), what are the TTLs and retention policies? Are values encrypted at rest?

If you have a short table or the CSV export, that would be helpful — we're trying to finalize our security questionnaire by Friday.

Hi Elena — thanks for the note. Attaching the requested export (redwood_subprocessors_2026Q3.csv) and a small diagram that maps request flows (edge-proxy-diagram.pdf). (attachment: redwood_subprocessors_2026Q3.csv - CSV; attachment: edge-proxy-diagram.pdf - PDF)

High-level answers up-front:
- Edge proxy / CDN: we use EdgeServ (EdgeServe Ops) as our edge ingress/egress provider in multiple regions. EdgeServ performs TCP/HTTP routing and short-lived caching for performance. They do not perform long-term storage of request payloads; logs are retained for 30 days for operational debugging and are stored in EdgeServ's US region by default.
- KV cache / session store: we use Cachely (contracted via Cachely Inc.) for ephemeral KV caching. Default TTLs are 1–6 hours depending on route; values are encrypted at rest (AES-256) and encrypted in transit. Persistent customer storage (model artifacts, user-provided content) is NOT stored in Cachely beyond the configured TTLs.

I looped in Priyom (infra) for the more technical details and Evelyn (legal) if you need DPA language or SOC 2 evidence. If helpful we can do a 30-minute call with our security/infra leads to walk through the CSV and diagrams.

Cheers,

Quick technical notes for the record (cc'ing legal & CS):
- EdgeServ: we use them as a reverse-proxy/edge router. They operate in a pass-through mode for request bodies; we only enable request caching for static assets and short-lived completion prefixes. Cache entries are TTL-based; default is 5 minutes for dynamic completions and up to 24 hours for static model artifacts (cached only in the EU when the route is pinned to eu-* regions).
- Logs retention: EdgeServ retains access logs for 30 days by default; we have a managed-log-export to our US logging bucket (S3) for 90 days when we enable advanced diagnostics for a customer (this is opt-in / on-demand).
- Cachely (KV): entries are AES-256 encrypted at rest, with per-customer namespaces. By default we set TTL = 6 hours for session / KV caches used in inference routing; we do NOT send KV contents to any external analytics vendors.

1) Aditya — please include the CSV row showing the regional data residency options and the checkbox for advanced diagnostics export.
2) Evelyn — can you confirm whether the DPA language around subprocessors and optional log export needs an explicit checkbox for BuyerCorp?
